Most transactions today clear as entries adjusted between banks.
adjusted: changed slightly to make something more suitable
The adjusted figures showed a smaller loss than first reported.
institutions: plural of institution: large, established organisations
Strong institutions help a country recover quickly from a crisis.
physical: relating to the body or the material world rather than the mind
Regular physical activity helps maintain a healthy heart and body.
handles: deals with or manages, third person singular
The airport handles millions of passengers every year.
shrinking: becoming smaller in size or amount
The town's population has been shrinking for the past decade.
minority: the smaller part of a group; a group that is smaller than the rest
Only a minority of residents supported the plan.
if: introducing a condition on which something depends
If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
anything: If you need anything during the trip, just call me.
outlasted: continued to exist for longer than something else
The old wooden bridge outlasted every replacement plan proposed for it.
about: The lecture was about how cities cope with extreme heat.
said: past tense of say; spoke or expressed something in words
She said the meeting would start at nine o'clock.
worth: having a value or deserving of something
Unless something marks it as worth keeping, it is allowed to fade.
saying: The sign at the entrance was saying the museum was closed.
presented: showed or offered something formally for consideration
The award was presented to the winning team by the mayor.
surprisingly: in a way that is unexpected
The exam was surprisingly easy compared to last year's version.
little: There is little time left before the deadline arrives.
support: help, encouragement or assistance given to someone
The charity offers support to families in financial difficulty.
we: used to refer to the speaker and one or more other people
We forget most of what we just learned within a day.
describe: to say what someone or something is like
Can you describe what happened right before the accident?
payments: amounts of money paid, or acts of paying
The company makes monthly payments to each of its suppliers.
may: The meeting may be postponed if too few people attend.
less: He eats less meat now than he used to.
clever: quick to understand and skilful at solving problems
It was a clever solution to a problem everyone else had ignored.
object: a physical thing that can be seen or touched
A strange object was found lying on the beach this morning.
invented: The printing press was invented in Europe in the fifteenth century.
score: a record of points earned in a game, test, or account
He checked the final score before leaving the stadium.
eventually: in the end, especially after a long process
Money may eventually have taken physical form from a simple scorekeeping habit.
took: past tense of take; obtained, seized, or required something
Computers took the jobs we thought were hardest, and left the ones a child can do.
form: to come into being or take shape
Ice crystals form quickly when the temperature drops below zero.
